text: NASA ordered Boeing's Starliner to return uncrewed because the five reaction-control system (RCS) thruster anomalies identified during docking could not be guaranteed safe for the deorbit burn, as these thrusters could not be ground-tested in their flight condition [Source: ev-1]. This decision meant that astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams remained aboard the International Space Station far longer than planned, returning on a Crew-9 Dragon roughly 9.5 months after launch instead of the planned ~8 days [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, under the fixed-price contract from NASA’s 2014 Commercial Crew program, Boeing had already incurred cumulative losses of more than $1.5 billion by 2025 compared to SpaceX's lower cost structure ($4.2B vs $2.6B total contracts respectively) [Source: ev-1].
